lines: Tool jokes work better when they have a <jump>point</jump>. Mine sometimes have two.
Tools jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with steel on them.
I keep a spare joke near the smithing table. It is not always ready for public use.
I told a joke at the smithing table once. The workstation took it better than the villagers did.
Toolsmith jokes need a good handle.
I had an axe joke, but it was too cutting.
A hammer joke lands with force and little subtlety.
My pickaxe joke digs itself deeper.
I told a shovel joke and it buried the room.
A grindstone joke can be a little abrasive.
The handle laughed, then split under pressure.
I know a wrench joke, but it twists badly.
A tool rack joke has a lot of support.
My chisel joke makes small points.
The hammer thinks every problem is a punchline.
I tried a repair joke. It worked better the second time.
A saw joke has teeth and questionable manners.
I asked the anvil for humor. It gave me impact.
The best tool joke is useful even when nobody laughs.
